description.text: Understand how net force and mass determine acceleration.

objectives.statement: Explain how net force and mass affect acceleration.
Calculate acceleration using a = F_net / m.

text.text: Two identical wheelbarrows are on the same level floor. You push both with the same net force. One is empty and the other is fully loaded. Which one accelerates more, and why?

content.alt: A person pushes a loaded wheelbarrow. Arrows show the applied force and acceleration, with F = ma and the relationships between force, mass, and acceleration.

caption.text: The same force produces greater acceleration when mass is smaller; increasing force increases acceleration.

text.text: The empty wheelbarrow accelerates more because the same net force acts on less mass. If the force increases while mass stays the same, acceleration increases. If the mass increases while force stays the same, acceleration decreases.

statement.text: For a constant-mass object, acceleration depends on net force and mass, and points in the direction of the net force.

caption.text: For constant mass, acceleration can be found using a = F_net / m.

conditions.text: Force is measured in newtons (N), mass in kilograms (kg), and acceleration in m/s^2.

prompt.text: A 5 kg box is pulled to the right by a net force of 20 N. What is its acceleration?

steps.description: Choose the form that finds acceleration.
Substitute the net force and mass.
Acceleration has the same direction as the net force.

answer.text: The box accelerates at 4 m/s^2 to the right.

text.text: Greater net force produces greater acceleration. Greater mass produces smaller acceleration for the same net force. Zero net force means zero acceleration, but the object may still move at constant velocity.

points.text: Acceleration points in the direction of the net force.
Use a = F_net / m for constant-mass objects.

prompt.text: A 10 kg object experiences a net force of 30 N. What is its acceleration?

feedback.text: a = F_net / m = 30 N / 10 kg = 3 m/s^2.

hint.text: Divide the net force by the mass.

prompt.text: The same net force acts on two objects. One has twice the mass of the other. Which object has greater acceleration?

feedback.text: Since a = F_net / m, the same force produces greater acceleration when the mass is smaller.

prompt.text: A car is moving east but slowing down. In which direction is its acceleration?

feedback.text: Acceleration points in the direction of the net force. To slow eastward motion, the acceleration must point west.

hint.text: Acceleration describes a change in velocity, not simply the direction of motion.

summary.text: Acceleration points in the direction of the net force.
Use a = F_net / m for constant-mass objects.
